newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine glistens with gold, diamonds - committee.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine glistens with gold, diamonds - committee.

text.p: Ukraine will begin commercial development of gold deposits soon and is confident that five other mining finds will sparkle with diamond deposits, senior officials from the State Geology Committee said on Thursday.
Serhy Hoshovsky, head of the State Geology Committee, said gold deposits were to be found practically all over Ukraine, but that the quantity of reserves was a state secret.
The committee's deputy head Dmytro Hursky said Ukraine had finally seen flashes of diamonds on its territory.

"In the last few years we have found five kimberlite pipes, which are being explored," he said. A small diamond was present in the Mriya (Dream) kimberlite pipe, an igneous rock formation that can bear diamonds, found last October.
He did not say what stage exploration was at, but said bringing one pipe to commercial development would cost hundreds of millions of dollars -- a problem for cash-strapped Ukraine.
Pipes had been located in the Zhytomyr, Khmelnytsky and Volyn regions in western Ukraine.
Officials said they planned to begin commercial gold exploitation at the Myzhiyevske deposit in the Carpathian mountains.
Ukrzoloto, the state gold concern, had been given licences to mine five gold fields and was also searching for new deposits, Hoshovsky said.
Ukrainian media previously have reported reserves of 40 to 50 tonnes of gold in developed fields.
Hursky said six developed gold deposits demonstrated "very high" gold content.
"At a minimum, according to our findings, there are 5.5 grams of gold for every tonne of ore, and some reserves demonstrate 10 grams per tonne," he said.
Industry Minister Valery Mazur said previously that 1997 would be the first year of gold mining in Ukraine.
Government statements have said that with proper financing Ukraine could produce annual gold volumes of 12 tonnes by 2001.
